episode_title: EP 53: Cognitive Surrender: The AI Engineering Mistake That Kills Projects

real_qa.q: What is cognitive surrender in AI engineering and how does it differ from cognitive offloading?
real_qa.r: Cognitive surrender is when you say just go do it without thinking about what the AI is doing or understanding its output. Cognitive offloading is different—it means asking Claude how edge caching works to learn and expand your own understanding. Ethan emphasizes that cognitive surrender leads to hallucinations and broken projects, while staying curious and asking why questions helps the AI reason better.

real_qa.q: How can BigQuery MCP connector mistakes impact user trust in AI data systems?
real_qa.r: When the BigQuery MCP connector went to the wrong product, dataset, or table and returned incorrect information, it sowed fear, uncertainty, and doubt in users. Once that trust is broken, you have to work twice as hard to get it back. Users then avoid using the system because verification takes three times as long and defeats the efficiency gains AI is supposed to provide.

real_qa.q: What is conversational analytics and how does it improve data accuracy for AI queries?
real_qa.r: Conversational analytics, which comes from Google, uses LookML to create agents trained on business metrics and calculated fields. When Ethan's team tested their MCP tool against Google's conversational analytics on the same questions, the conversational analytics got it right 100% of the time because the agent was trained to identify exactly what users were trying to do, compared to their earlier 30-70% accuracy.

real_qa.q: Why is semantic layer and documentation critical before building AI data systems?
real_qa.r: Claude cannot reliably query across thousands of projects without knowing which ones are production-level or what data users should access. Organizations that have documented every field and table in their databases give Claude context to work with. Without this hard work of documentation and building a semantic layer with LookML, Claude will guess and return wrong answers, breaking user trust.
real_qa.requete: semantic layer data documentation AI accuracy

real_qa.q: What step-by-step approach prevents cognitive surrender when building AI systems?
real_qa.r: Start with a long voice conversation asking Claude why it would do things a certain way, really understanding its thinking. Keep asking why like a child to correct its reasoning. Then ask Claude what it doesn't know about requirements that would be important. Once you feel confident, stop and go back to text to get all requirements in a visual format, refine the architecture, and only then build.
real_qa.requete: avoid cognitive surrender AI project approach
